originalTitle: Next OpenAIs and Anthropics may come straight to retail market. Here's what to know before investing
summary: The SEC wants retail investors to access private markets, and with all the hype around tech darlings going public, there's plenty of potential reward and risk.
content:
Amid ongoing hype around tech darlings going public , from Anthropic to OpenAI , many retail investors are chomping at the bit for access to private stock markets.

Investing in private companies has traditionally been reserved for more sophisticated investors, but there are ways retail investors can participate. This goes beyond being lucky enough to work for a private company that's doling out shares or participating in an investment round for friends and family.

The trend is set to accelerate as the Securities and Exchange Commission commits to a policy of offering more ways for retail investors to access investments traditionally off limits to them. This week, SEC chairman Paul Atkins said that in response to investor demand, the SEC is issuing new proposals to make sure that these investments are "not be reserved for the wealthiest or for those deemed to be the most sophisticated."

The SEC proposals include permitting registered investment advisers to charge performance fees of up to 20% on public funds — a level comparable to fees historically used in the hedge fund and alternatives space. The SEC is also considering new ways for individual investors to qualify for access to private market investments associated with "accredited investors" — including passing an exam .

Already, there are about two dozen publicly available closed-end funds focused on private equity or venture capital, according to Morningstar Direct. "It's a way to get private market exposure without getting too much exposure to one company," said Emily Zheng, senior research analyst at PitchBook, a Morningstar company.

There are also ETFs in the market that straddle the line between public stock holdings and private companies.

Here's what investors need to know about investing in these types of funds, and what they can learn from these funds about a future in which more of what has been traditionally private becomes accessible to more of the investing public.

Inherently risky, longer timelines, less financial info

Private equity generally focuses on established businesses looking for restructuring or growth capital, whereas venture capital targets high-growth-potential early-stage startups. Either way, these investments are inherently risky and have longer investment timelines.

The private companies held within publicly traded funds are illiquid, and there can be a disconnect between the worth of the underlying securities and what individual investors are willing to pay for the funds. Some of the funds are only available through select brokerages, and investment minimums may apply. Though there's a lot of focus on how to make money by investing in private companies right now, investors have to be careful, financial advisors say.

Which fund or funds you buy can depend on what your brokerage offers.

Sofi , for example, offers access to certain funds that may not be available through other brokerages. Private and venture funds on Sofi's platform include the ARK Venture Fund ( ARKVX ), the CAZ GP Stakes Fund ( CZGIX ) and the Cashmere Fund ( CSHMX ). Other funds, like the Robinhood Ventures Fund 1 ( RVI ), the Destiny Tech100 Closed End Fund ( DXYZ ) and the Fundrise Innovation Fund ( VCX ) can be purchased at brokerages such as Robinhood and Fidelity.

Before buying a private equity or VC fund, it's important to check which companies the funds hold, especially if you want access to certain well-known private companies on the verge of going public or that have expressed plans for an eventual IPO. ARK Venture, for example, held OpenAI and Anthropic as part of its top-10 holdings as of Aug. 31. Robinhood Ventures Fund 1's top holdings include fintechs Ramp and Revolut, and OpenAI.

Keep in mind, you won't have financials to look at for many of the portfolio holdings because they're private companies, and often, there's not a lot of public information on the companies within these funds, especially if they are early start-ups. "You can find a lot more information about OpenAI than a company that's just starting out," Zheng said. "You have to be okay with that and know it's a risk you're taking."

If you may need to cash out next year, don't invest

Because the assets in these funds aren't liquid, an investor's timeline is an important consideration, said Adrianna Adams, head of financial planning at New York-based financial planning firm Domain Money. "They are meant to be long-term investments," she said. "If you want liquidity the next year, the investment hasn't really had the chance to get going yet."

With any fund under consideration, investors should check the policies for cashing out. Can they buy and sell like any other stock, or only a certain percentage each quarter?

On the debt side of things, that has been a big issue in private credit this year, with many investors stampeding for the exits and being blocked by big alternative investment fund managers based on prospectus rules for redemptions.

Investors should also consider their goals for the money and whether they can afford to lose their investment. Also, can they stomach the volatility associated with these funds? If clients have enough income to recover from a loss and it wouldn't hurt their goals, Adams said she wouldn't object to them investing.

Investors need to be aware that fees in private equity and VC funds are typically significantly higher than index funds or ETFs made up of public company stocks, said Rami Sarafa, chief executive at Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York. Expense ratios for these funds can be in the 3% to upper 4% range. Also, some investors may pay higher fees depending on the brokerage they purchase the fund from, Sarafa said.

Among ETFs that can give investors some exposure to private companies, it remains minimal comparatively, based on SEC rules limiting net assets in illiquid investments to no more than 15% of a public fund.

chineseTitle: 接下来 OpenAI 和 Anthropics 可能会直接进入零售市场。这是投资前需要了解的内容
chineseSummary: 美国证券交易委员会希望散户投资者进入私人市场，随着围绕科技宠儿上市的所有炒作，存在大量潜在回报和风险。
chineseContent:
在围绕从 Anthropic 到 OpenAI 等科技宠儿上市的持续炒作中，许多散户投资者都在争先恐后地进入私人股票市场。

传统上，投资私营公司是为更成熟的投资者保留的，但散户投资者可以通过多种方式参与。这不仅仅是幸运地为一家为朋友和家人发放股票或参与一轮投资的私人公司工作。

随着美国证券交易委员会致力于为散户投资者提供更多传统上禁止投资的方式，这一趋势必将加速。本周，美国证券交易委员会主席保罗·阿特金斯表示，为了满足投资者的需求，美国证券交易委员会正在发布新的提案，以确保这些投资“不会保留给最富有的人或那些被认为是最有经验的人”。

SEC 的提议包括允许注册投资顾问对公共基金收取高达 20% 的业绩费——这一水平与对冲基金和另类投资领域历史上使用的费用相当。美国证券交易委员会还在考虑让个人投资者有资格获得与“合格投资者”相关的私募市场投资的新方法，包括通过考试。

据 Morningstar Direct 称，目前已有约两打公开发售的封闭式基金专注于私募股权或风险投资。晨星公司 PitchBook 的高级研究分析师艾米丽·郑 (Emily Cheng) 表示：“这是一种获得私募市场风险敞口的方式，而无需过多投资一家公司。”

市场上也有跨越公共股票持有和私人公司持股之间界限的 ETF。

以下是投资者在投资此类基金时需要了解的信息，以及他们可以从这些基金中学到的关于未来的信息，在未来，更多传统上私人的东西将被更多的投资公众所接受。

固有风险、时间较长、财务信息较少

私募股权通常专注于寻求重组或成长资本的成熟企业，而风险投资则针对高增长潜力的早期初创企业。无论哪种方式，这些投资本质上都是有风险的，并且投资期限较长。

公开交易基金中持有的私人公司缺乏流动性，基础证券的价值与个人投资者愿意为基金支付的价格之间可能存在脱节。部分资金只能通过精选经纪商获得，并且可能存在最低投资额。财务顾问表示，尽管目前人们非常关注如何通过投资私营公司赚钱，但投资者必须小心。

您购买哪种基金取决于您的经纪公司提供的服务。

例如，Sofi 提供对其他经纪公司可能无法提供的某些资金的访问权。 Sofi 平台上的私募和风险基金包括 ARK Venture Fund (ARKVX)、CAZ GP Stakes Fund (CZGIX) 和 Cashmere Fund (CSHMX)。其他基金，如 Robinhood Ventures Fund 1 (RVI)、Destiny Tech100 Closed End Fund (DXYZ) 和 Fundrise Innovation Fund (VCX) 可以在 Robinhood 和 Fidelity 等经纪公司购买。

在购买私募股权或风险投资基金之前，检查基金持有哪些公司非常重要，特别是如果您想接触某些即将上市或已表示最终计划进行 IPO 的知名私营公司。例如，截至 8 月 31 日，ARK Venture 持有 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 作为其前 10 名持股的一部分。Robinhood Ventures Fund 1 的主要持仓包括金融科技公司 Ramp 和 Revolut 以及 OpenAI。

请记住，您无需查看许多投资组合持股的财务信息，因为它们是私营公司，而且通常，这些基金中的公司的公开信息并不多，特别是如果它们是早期初创企业的话。 “与一家刚刚起步的公司相比，你可以找到更多有关 OpenAI 的信息，”郑说。 “你必须接受这一点，并且知道这是你正在冒的风险。”

如果您明年可能需要套现，请不要投资

纽约财务规划公司 Domain Money 的财务规划主管阿德里安娜·亚当斯 (Adrianna Adams) 表示，由于这些基金中的资产缺乏流动性，因此投资者的时间表是一个重要的考虑因素。 “它们应该是长期投资，”她说。 “如果你想要明年的流动性，那么投资还没有真正开始的机会。”

对于任何正在考虑的基金，投资者应检查兑现政策。他们可以像其他股票一样买卖，还是每个季度只能按一定比例买卖？

在债务方面，这一直是今年私人信贷的一个大问题，许多投资者争先恐后地退出，并被大型另类投资基金经理根据招股说明书的赎回规则阻止。

投资者还应该考虑他们的资金目标以及他们是否能够承受损失投资的损失。此外，他们能承受与这些基金相关的波动吗？亚当斯表示，如果客户有足够的收入来弥补损失，并且不会损害他们的目标，她不会反对他们投资。

纽约 Cordoba Advisory Partners 首席执行官拉米·萨拉法 (Rami Sarafa) 表示，投资者需要意识到，私募股权和风险投资基金的费用通常明显高于指数基金或由上市公司股票组成的 ETF。这些基金的费用比率可以在 3% 到 4% 以上的范围内。萨拉法表示，此外，一些投资者可能会支付更高的费用，具体取决于他们购买基金的经纪公司。

根据美国证券交易委员会 (SEC) 的规定，非流动性投资的净资产不得超过公共基金的 15%，因此在可以为投资者提供一定程度的私营公司投资的 ETF 中，这一比例仍然相对较低。
